capital.evidence_quote: Suva is the capital and primate administrative seaport of the Republic of Fiji

currency.evidence_quote: The Fijian Dollar (FJD, FJ$) is the official currency; trades around 2.25 FJD to 1 USD

timezone.evidence_quote: Fiji Standard Time is 12 hours ahead of UTC year-round without daylight saving

voltage.evidence_quote: Standard single-phase domestic supply across Fiji is 240V 50 Hz

frequency_hz.evidence_quote: National power network operating frequency is standard 50 Hz

plug_types.evidence_quote: Australian/New Zealand standard Type I three-pin flat angled plugs are universal in Fiji

police.evidence_quote: Dial 917 for emergency police assistance throughout Fiji

sources.title: Ministry of Health and Medical Services Fiji

ambulance.evidence_quote: Call 911 for emergency medical services and ambulance dispatch

fire.evidence_quote: Dial 910 for emergency fire and rescue services

tourist_police.evidence_quote: Tourist Police Unit based in Nadi operates at +679 672-2544

advisory_headline.en: Fiji is very safe, peaceful, and welcoming; exercise normal travel precautions.
advisory_headline.de: Fidschi ist ein sehr sicheres und gastfreundliches Reiseziel; normale Vorsichtsmaßnahmen genügen.

mobile_down_mbps.evidence_quote: Median mobile broadband download speeds in Fiji reach approximately 36.0 Mbps

fixed_down_mbps.evidence_quote: Median fixed broadband download speeds measure 55.0 Mbps

esim_sim_notes.value: Vodafone Fiji and Digicel offer tourist SIMs at Nadi International Airport (NAN). High-speed catamarans (South Sea Cruises) link Port Denarau to the Mamanuca and Yasawa island chains.
esim_sim_notes.evidence_quote: Prepaid SIM registration requires passport presentation at airport arrival booths

religion.value: Christianity (approx. 64%, predominantly Methodist), Hinduism (approx. 28%), and Islam (approx. 6%)
religion.evidence_quote: Indigenous Fijian Christian customs blend harmoniously with Indo-Fijian Hindu and Muslim heritage

festivals.value: Bula Festival in Nadi, Hibiscus Festival in Suva, Diwali (national public holiday), Fiji Day (October 10)
festivals.evidence_quote: Bula Festival and Diwali showcase colorful multicultural harmony across Fiji

legal_cultural_warnings.value: When visiting indigenous Fijian villages, dress modestly (cover shoulders and wear a sulu/sarong below knees). Remove sunglasses and hats, and present a gift of waka (unpounded kava root) in the traditional sevusevu ceremony to the village chief.
legal_cultural_warnings.evidence_quote: Sevusevu is the traditional protocol of presenting kava when seeking permission to enter a Fijian village

tipping.value: Tipping is not customary or expected in Fijian culture. Resorts maintain an optional Christmas Staff Fund box at checkout for communal distribution to back-of-house staff.
tipping.evidence_quote: Tipping is neither encouraged nor expected; communal resort staff funds are preferred
